reason: The arithmetic reproduces (150 bets/41 games; CLV +2.83% on 95 closes/35 games [+1.98, +3.92]; ROI -3.39%; independent closes +0.45% on 26; within-day permutation p 0.063), and there is no look-ahead in the construction (each bet is priced at the first in-window look with EV>=2.5% using only that look; closes are used only to score it). But as a RULE it is not a credible improvement over R1: (1) its gain over R1 is +0.28 pts of average CLV (R1 +2.54%), bought by dropping 34 of 184 entries that themselves beat the close on average (+1.27%); (2) 69% of its closes are Tracker closes (CNO's own consensus, placed bets only) where CLV just equals the listed EV; the independent closes show +0.45% on 26 closes/18 games (CI includes 0) and the plus-vs-favourite gap reverses sign on Novig-trades closes (-0.85 pts) and on all non-tracker closes in R1 (+0.45% plus vs +2.15% favourites, 26 vs 7); controlling for close source the gap is +0.88 pts [-0.28, +2.56] (p 0.08) and stratified permutation p = 0.24; (3) it cannot be date-split: the second half has 46 bets in 6 games, 16 closes in 4 games (all tracker closes of bets Tj placed) and only 2 favourite closes in 2 games, so the plus-vs-favourite contrast has no out-of-sample test; the gap sits on Oct 4 (15 favourite closes/8 games, +0.71% vs plus +2.73%) while Oct 3 shows plus +2.43% vs favourites +2.44% (4 closes); the builder's half numbers (+2.43/+2.91%) do not reproduce; (4) one of 522 rules tried (the raw p 0.006 is not near any multiple-comparison bar). What is real: in the wide population (378 closes/59 games) CLV falls about 0.8-0.9 pts per +0.10 of implied probability at equal EV even after controlling for close source and on independent closes (-0.79 [-1.50, -0.08]), so the PRICE effect is plausible and worth tracking as a hypothesis; it is not yet an action. As a question for Tj only (never as a change): 'should the auto-bet's accepted price range narrow from -200..+130 to +100..+130?' (a tightening, not a loosening) would be settled by about 120 more games of independent-source closes (gap of 1 pt at 80% power, SE 0.55 pts at 51 games now) which at 18 games/day is about 7 more study days (only the closes from Novig trades, ESPN and Pinnacle count; tracker closes do not); until then keep logging, do not change a rule that decides which bets are placed.
caveats: Tracker closes (CNO's books, or Vigilant's fair line, read before the start) exist only for bets Tj placed; they measure whether CNO's own consensus moved, not the market: against them CLV ~ listed EV (R2: EV 3.64%, drift +0.11%, CLV +3.74%). The 'beat the close' evidence for R2 is therefore 69% circular.
Closes exist for 95 of 150 R2 bets (63%); the 55 without a close are 49 props (cost 0.41 average vs 0.47 for those with a close): the CLV describes the placed / near-start subset, not the 150.

Game-cluster CIs resample 35 games for R2 CLV (41 entries' games) and 40 games for plus-vs-favourite; the second half has 4 games with closes: its CI [+3.3%, +4.6%] is an artefact of 4 clusters, do not quote it.

Plus money here is almost entirely cost 0.46-0.50 (+100 to +117; 73 of 95 closes): only 3 closes sit below cost 0.42, so the rule says nothing about longshots; favourites are cost 0.50-0.55 (17 of 21 closes).

Props are 80 of R2's 95 closes (NFL 65, NHL 19): the result is a prop / NFL-and-NHL result of two game days (Oct 3-5), with app versions 0.57-0.68 and presets changing underneath (CLV by version ranges +0.07% (0.60.0, 14 closes) to +4.7%).

Look-price CLV (+2.83%) differs from first-listed CLV (+1.92%) because the rule waits for the EV >= 2.5% look; 55% of chosen looks are later than the bet's first look, and each needs the app to see and buy at that look's price (median Novig $ available at the first-listed price is only $47).
I could not reproduce the builder's 'baseline CLV 1.98%' nor the builder's date-half CLVs (2.43% / 2.91%); the other numbers match to the digit or within bootstrap noise.
Any change to which bets are placed is a question for Tj, not an action; the evidence suggests only that the price hypothesis deserves more data.
